It's been years since I fucked with anything that eats Windows like that, but basically what you need to do is find out where in the registry your shell is defined and fix that. The whole key may be gone, or it might be empty, or it may be referring to some executable that no longer exists. Fix that, and you'll be... workable.

Windows will never be what it was after an incident like this, though. Bottom line is, you're screwed. You can try to do an overlay, just reinstall Windows over the top of the existing install and hope for the best, but that has become less and less effective with newer versions of Windows, so depending on what you're running, this may fail catastrophically. The best solution for you, if you're married to Windows, is backup and reinstall.

Of course, you can just stick with ctrl+shift+esc, new task, explorer, and hope that nothing else breaks, but it eventually will. There's also the option of taking this opportunity to simply ditch Windows entirely. Good luck!
